unit.why: An anthology section of teachings on love of friends, gemilut hasadim and hospitality (Yesod ha-Avodah, R. Elimelekh's 'three pillars', the Apter Rav's homily on escorting guests, Jacob crossing his hands). Three short narratives are embedded in it: two Talmudic anecdotes from Ketubot 67 and one Hasidic anecdote about R. Moshe of Przeworsk.
unit.boundary_note: The Przeworsk anecdote is cut in the middle by a long editor's footnote (המאסף) and resumes after it with 'אורח. וז״פ עוה״ז דומה לפרוזדור'. The anthology on gemilut hasadim continues into the next division.

stories.start_quote: אמרו עליו על הלל הזקן שלקח
stories.summary_en: Hillel the Elder provided an impoverished man of good family with a horse and a servant, and once, finding no servant, ran before him himself for three miles.

stories.start_quote: האי דאתי לקמיה דרבא א״ל במה
stories.summary_en: A poor man asks Rava for fattened chicken and old wine, citing God's provision of each person's food in its time. Just then Rava's sister, unseen for thirteen years, arrives bearing exactly those foods, and Rava concedes.

stories.start_quote: ונוראות שמעתי על הה״ק א״א ר׳ משה מפרשעווארסק
stories.summary_en: A guest rebuked R. Moshe of Przeworsk, author of Or Penei Moshe, for having no benches in his house. The rebbe asked why the guest had none, the guest replied that he was only a passing traveller, and the rebbe answered that he too is a traveller, since this world is only a corridor.

quotes: שהוכיחו אורח על שאין לו ספסלין בביתו
